# sysutils_users (Data Source)

Lists the user accounts in `/etc/passwd`, optionally filtered by name, uid range, primary group and login shell. With the provider's `root_dir` set, `/etc/passwd` is read below `root_dir`.

The data source parses `/etc/passwd` directly, with the same parser as the [`provider::sysutils::parse_passwd_line`](../functions/parse_passwd_line.md) function. Unlike the [`sysutils_user`](./user.md) data source, which looks up one account through the name service switch (NSS), it does not list accounts provided only by directory services such as LDAP or SSSD, which usually cannot be enumerated anyway. Blank lines, comments and NIS compat entries (lines starting with `+` or `-`) are skipped. The data source does not require root privileges.

All filters are optional and combine with AND; without any, every entry is returned. An empty result is not an error.

The data source is read during planning, so accounts that [`sysutils_user`](../resources/user.md) resources in the same configuration create are only listed if the data source depends on them, for example with `depends_on`.

## Example Usage

### List regular users

```terraform
# Regular login users: uids from 1000 up (the usual UID_MIN in
# /etc/login.defs), excluding the "nobody" account.
data "sysutils_users" "humans" {
  uid_min = 1000
  uid_max = 60000
}

output "human_users" {
  value = data.sysutils_users.humans.names
}

output "human_homes" {
  value = { for u in data.sysutils_users.humans.users : u.name => u.home }
}
```

### Act on every user with a given shell

```terraform
# Every account whose login shell is bash ...
data "sysutils_users" "bash" {
  shell = "/bin/bash"
}

# ... gets a shared profile snippet in its home directory.
resource "sysutils_file" "bash_aliases" {
  for_each = {
    for u in data.sysutils_users.bash.users : u.name => u
    if u.uid >= 1000
  }

  path    = "${each.value.home}/.bash_aliases"
  content = "alias ll='ls -l'\n"
  owner   = each.key
  mode    = "0644"
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `gid` (Number) Only return users whose primary group has this gid.
- `name_regex` (String) Only return entries whose name matches this [RE2 regular expression](https://github.com/google/re2/wiki/Syntax). The expression matches anywhere in the name unless it is anchored, so use `^...$` to match whole names.
- `shell` (String) Only return users with exactly this login shell, for example `/bin/bash`. An empty string matches entries that leave the shell empty.
- `uid_max` (Number) Only return users whose uid is at most this value. Must not be less than `uid_min`.
- `uid_min` (Number) Only return users whose uid is at least this value.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Data source identifier (always `/etc/passwd`).
- `names` (List of String) The names of the matching users, in the same order as `users`.
- `users` (Attributes List) The matching users, in the order of `/etc/passwd`. Entries that share a name or uid are all listed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--users))

<a id="nestedatt--users"></a>
### Nested Schema for `users`

Read-Only:

- `comment` (String) The complete GECOS comment field. An empty string if the field is empty.
- `gid` (Number) Numeric ID of the user's primary group.
- `home` (String) Home directory.
- `name` (String) Username.
- `shell` (String) Login shell. An empty string if the entry leaves it empty, which login programs treat as `/bin/sh`.
- `uid` (Number) Numeric user ID.

## Errors

| Situation | Diagnostic |
|-----------|------------|
| `name_regex` is not a valid regular expression | `Invalid regular expression` |
| `uid_min` is greater than `uid_max` | `Invalid uid range` |
| `/etc/passwd` is missing, cannot be read, is larger than 64 MiB, or its path leads outside `root_dir` | `Reading passwd database` |
| `/etc/passwd` contains a line that is not a valid entry (not seven fields, an empty name, or a uid or gid that is not a number) | `Reading passwd database`, with the line number |

## Caveats

- The password field is never exposed; it is `x` on almost every system anyway, with the hash in `/etc/shadow`.
- The whole list is stored in the state and shown in plans. On hosts with many local accounts, narrow it down with the filters.
- With the provider's `root_dir` set, symlinks such as an absolute `etc/passwd` link are resolved inside `root_dir`, as a chrooted process would; a link leading above `root_dir` is an error.
- The data source only works on Unix-like systems.
